newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends volatile day up on BOK comments.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends volatile day up on BOK comments.

text.p: The won ended Tuesday's trading higher against the U.S. currency, boosted by news the central Bank of Korea (BOK) would seek "strong steps" to stabilise the falling won, traders said.

The currency started the day weak due to import settlements, falling to a new 84-month low of 887.00 won. But the BOK's comments of strong steps against won's depreciation helped the won rebound to close at 870.50 from Monday's close of 880.00
"The BOK is trying to stabilise the won at around the 870 level," said a western bank dealer. "In short-term it may work, but there is no fundamental reason for the dollar to go down."

A senior BOK official told reporters on Tuesday that the dollar's surge looked extremely "abnormal" and was not at all helpful to the South Korean economy. The monetary authority will take "strong measures which are different from the past," he said.
The central bank's repeated dollar selling also served to support the won, traders said.

A finance ministry official said the government was considering various steps as a way of supporting won, including raising the foreign stockholdings ceiling earlier than planned. Seoul has said it would raise the limit to 23 percent from 20 percent some time this year, but no date has been set.
